statusDetail: Coverage-complete agentic audit across six representative paths. Sports other than football were not separately audited because they share the score-list template; authentication, checkout, and account flows were not exposed in the public surfaces.

page.notes: Server-rendered metadata/content with hydrated live-score interactions, a registered service worker, mandatory age choice, and a consent-management layer.

paths.description: Homepage and live-score listing, the primary score-discovery journey and shared application chrome.
Match-detail archetype, representing live event detail pages.
News listing archetype, representing editorial discovery and non-JavaScript crawlability.
News article archetype, representing long-form content and share/structured metadata.
Settings and privacy-management surface, representing an interactive preference flow.
Intentional unknown route, representing HTTP failure and recovery behavior.

findings.summary: The interface is hard-coded to a dark palette rather than responding to the system theme.
findings.evidence: The platform probe reports computed color-scheme "normal" and the dark-emulation capture does not establish any preference-driven retinting; no color-scheme declaration was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and use prefers-color-scheme or light-dark() tokens so surfaces follow the user preference.

findings.summary: Animations continue when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the active probe found two running animations, each with a 1000 ms duration, and zero reduced-motion CSS rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a prefers-reduced-motion: reduce branch that removes non-essential animation and transitions while preserving state cues.

findings.summary: Full-viewport age and privacy gates obscure the primary score content on arrival.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show the score experience fully covered by either an age gate or a privacy panel. The interruption probe measured a fixed 780x493 element covering the full 780x493 viewport and body overflow hidden.
findings.suggestedFix: Keep legally required choices concise and accessible, preserve an immediate content preview where allowed, and implement the modal with the native dialog primitive and clear dismiss/decision paths.

findings.summary: The blocking age experience is a custom fixed div rather than a semantic modal.
findings.evidence: The interruption probe found a full-screen fixed DIV and the modern UI probe found zero dialog elements, popovers, or aria-modal dialogs.
findings.suggestedFix: Use <dialog> with showModal(), autofocus/focus restoration, Escape handling, and a labelled heading for the blocking age decision.

findings.summary: Reusable score components appear to depend on viewport rules rather than container-level adaptation.
findings.evidence: The platform probe found zero CSS container rules despite reusable match, league, navigation, and footer components rendered in several widths.
findings.suggestedFix: Give reusable cards and navigation regions containment and apply @container rules where their composition changes with available component space.

findings.summary: Several controls are too small for touch and the first focused link has no visible outline style.
findings.evidence: The interaction probe found favourite buttons rendered at 16x16 px and multiple controls at 40x40 px. The focused first link computed to outline-style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide at least 44x44 CSS pixel hit areas (spacing can count), add a strong :focus-visible treatment, and retain non-hover affordances.

findings.summary: The throttled load misses the good LCP range.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP at 11.4 s, Speed Index at 5.3 s, TBT at 240 ms, and a performance score of 0.67. A separate unthrottled trace measured LCP at 2.434 s, showing a material slow-network sensitivity.
findings.suggestedFix: Profile the LCP element, prioritize its required resource, cut critical dependency depth, and defer non-essential scripts using the performance guidance.

findings.summary: A script-heavy dependency chain and third-party payload delay useful rendering.
findings.evidence: The HAR records 102 requests and 1,161,947 transferred bytes, including 43 scripts (609,529 bytes), 11 stylesheets, and 355,212 third-party bytes. Lighthouse flags the network dependency tree.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial route chunks, load advertising/measurement after consent and idle, consolidate critical CSS, and keep deferred scripts out of the LCP chain.

findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails button-name and link-name. The DOM probe identifies two date-navigation anchors containing only SVG with no aria-label or meaningful text.
findings.suggestedFix: Add concise accessible names to icon-only links/buttons and verify all controls expose the intended name and role in the accessibility tree.

findings.summary: Heading order and keyboard focus presentation are not robust.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails heading-order and accessibility-tree checks; the rendered heading sequence jumps from H1 to H4, and the first focused link has outline-style none.
findings.suggestedFix: Use sequential semantic headings and landmarks, and define an unmistakable :focus-visible ring for every interactive control.

findings.summary: The viewport metadata restricts user zoom.
findings.evidence: The match probe shows maximum-scale=1.0 and Lighthouse fails meta-viewport because maximum-scale is less than 5.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and any user-scalable restriction so users can zoom while retaining the existing responsive reflow.

findings.summary: Some images are served at unsuitable dimensions or aspect ratios.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse fails image-aspect-ratio and image-size-responsive; the image probe reports 23 of 32 images as oversized and 21 in legacy PNG format.
findings.suggestedFix: Serve correctly cropped responsive image variants with width/height, srcset/sizes, and modern formats while preserving intrinsic aspect ratio.

findings.summary: Important browser security headers are missing and the consent cookie lacks Secure.
findings.evidence: The headers primitive reports no Content-Security-Policy, no X-Content-Type-Options, and no Referrer-Policy. The OptanonConsent cookie is not Secure. HTTPS, HSTS, X-Frame-Options, and Permissions-Policy are present.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a restrictive CSP, nosniff, and an explicit Referrer-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and retain SameSite protections.

findings.summary: The pre-consent page has a large third-party and partner footprint.
findings.evidence: The privacy UI names 745 partners. Network evidence records 32 third-party requests and 355,212 third-party bytes, including Permutive and GeoEdge scripts; the tracker probe sees nine third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Default to data minimisation, gate advertising and measurement tags until an informed choice, reduce partner count, and batch only necessary analytics.

findings.summary: Core live-score content is not usable without JavaScript.
findings.evidence: The no-JavaScript crawler screenshot replaces the score list with an out-of-date/disabled-browser warning and a legacy-site link. Discoverability coverage is only 48%, although title, H1, and some server-rendered text remain.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render the current score list and core navigation as functional HTML, then hydrate enhancements; retain the legacy link only as a fallback.

findings.summary: The stylesheet relies overwhelmingly on physical left/right properties.
findings.evidence: Across readable stylesheets, the CSS probe counted hundreds of physical left/right declarations but only 17 logical-property occurrences. The document does correctly declare lang=en and dir=ltr and exposes 18 localized alternates.
findings.suggestedFix: Migrate directional spacing, sizing, and positioning to logical inline/block properties and regression-test the Arabic locale in RTL.

findings.summary: Rejecting partner processing is presented as “Pay to Reject”.
findings.evidence: The mobile privacy screenshot gives equal visual prominence to “I Accept” and “Pay to Reject”, while describing 745 partners and blocking the news content until a choice is made.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer a free, equally prominent reject-non-essential option with neutral wording; separate any paid ad-free product from the consent decision.

findings.summary: Image delivery is not consistently resolution- or format-efficient.
findings.evidence: The image probe marks 23 of 32 images oversized, five without responsive srcset, and 21 using legacy formats. A stadium image alone transfers 163,490 bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate right-sized AVIF/WebP variants, use srcset/sizes, and avoid downloading decorative stadium art at a larger resolution than rendered.

findings.summary: Third-party scripts consume a disproportionate share of the initial route budget.
findings.evidence: Third parties account for 355,212 of 1,161,947 transferred bytes; Permutive and GeoEdge scripts are two of the three largest non-image resources and load on the initial route.
findings.suggestedFix: Delay non-essential third-party execution until consent and idle/interaction, remove low-value vendors, and enforce a route-level third-party byte budget.

taskList.title: Remove consent coercion and reduce the pre-consent partner footprint
Restore zoom, control names, focus visibility, and touch target sizing
Cut the initial script/dependency chain and optimize LCP
Add CSP, nosniff, Referrer-Policy, and secure cookie attributes
Server-render usable current scores for no-JavaScript resilience
Make required overlays semantic and less obstructive
Honor system theme and reduced-motion preferences
Modernize image sizing, formats, and responsive delivery
Adopt container queries and logical properties
